newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller warns Iran on Kurd rebels.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller warns Iran on Kurd rebels.

text.p: Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller said on Sunday she had warned Iran to halt its alleged support for Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels fighting for self-rule in southeast Turkey.

"Turkey can no longer turn a blind eye to this," state-run Anatolian news agency quoted Ciller as saying. "We warned our friends in a brotherly manner," she said in reference to a meeting she had with Iranian counterpart Ali Akbar Velayati in the western Turkish city of Izmir on Saturday.
"Every day martyrs are dying on our borders. We cannot accept this," Ciller said.

Six Turkish soldiers died last week in an attack on a border post by Kurdish rebels who Turkish officials said came from Iran. At the weekend Turkish officials said soldiers killed 33 Kurdish rebels in Van province near the border with Iran.

The number of attacks near the border have increased in recent weeks. Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said during a visit to Iran last month that Tehran assured him it was not supporting the separatist group.
"You say there are no terrorists (in Iran). Where are they coming from? From nowhere?" said Ciller, Erbakan's pro-Western coalition partner.
Velayati, in Turkey for a meeting of an Islamic economic group, met President Suleyman Demirel on Sunday, Anatolian said.
Ciller urged Iran to take action against the PKK, jointly with Turkey if necesary, or let Ankara sort out the border problem itself.
"If you don't do it, let us do it. If you don't want that then we can do it together," she said.

More than 20,000 people have died in 12 years of fighting between the PKK and the Turkish army. Turkey also accuses neighbour Syria of sponsoring the guerrillas and has said it wants to set up a "security zone" just across the border in northern Iraq to stop rebel infiltration from that country.
